headline: Kai, the AI trade is being repriced for the cost of money: the chip index fell 6.7 percent, the ten-year dropped to 4.95 percent, and Brent is above $114.
subline: Meta's free cash flow went negative for the first time since it went public, Anthropic may make its S-1 public today, and flash PMIs land at 9:45.
asof: Pre-market · quotes 4:00–6:45 AM ET · index figures are futures · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Chip index posts worst day since June
items.sentence: The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index fell 6.7 percent on Thursday, its steepest drop since June 23, with Intel, AMD, Sandisk and Marvell each down more than 8 percent, per Reuters.

items.title: Meta's free cash flow turns negative
items.sentence: FXStreet reports that $34.9 billion of third-quarter capital spending outran $32.8 billion of operating cash flow for minus $2.1 billion in free cash flow, Meta's first negative quarter since it went public, with full-year capex now guided to $135 to $145 billion.

items.title: Brent above $114 as freight costs bite
items.sentence: Brent traded at $114.73, up 0.9 percent after a 4 percent jump the session before, and Euronews notes that shipping crude from the Gulf to Asia now costs over $37 a barrel, more than five times the pre-war level.

items.title: Ten-year yield slides on a flight to Treasuries
items.sentence: Fortune reports the ten-year Treasury yield fell to about 4.9 percent from a recent peak above 5.30 percent as traders treated Treasuries as the safe haven during the tech selloff.

items.title: Flash PMIs and Michigan sentiment today
items.sentence: Trading Economics lists S&P Global's flash manufacturing and services PMIs at 9:45 AM ET and the final October Michigan sentiment reading at 10:00, with the Fed's rate decision due Wednesday, October 28.

items.title: Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia keep crude bid
items.sentence: Reuters reports crude held near five-month highs on concern over further supply disruption after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, with a pipeline valve also shutting in output at Libya's Hamada and Tahara fields.

items.title: Putin agrees to resume three-way Ukraine talks
items.sentence: PBS NewsHour reports Putin agreed in principle to restart Russia-Ukraine-US talks after November 10 following a three-hour meeting with Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg, while overnight strikes killed five people and wounded 25 across Ukraine.

items.title: France's ten-year yield tops 5 percent
items.sentence: Axios reports the French ten-year reached 5.01 percent, a post-2002 high and about 1.6 points above German bunds for the widest gap in fifteen years, which leaves France paying more to borrow for a decade than Washington does.

items.title: Democrats hold a nine-point generic-ballot lead
items.sentence: Forbes cites the Silver Bulletin average at 49.7 percent to 41.1 percent, an 8.6-point edge, with the Michigan, Iowa and Maine Senate races each polling inside two points.

items.title: Gucci sales fall and Kering drops 10 percent
items.sentence: Euronews reports Kering fell more than 10 percent after Gucci's third-quarter sales declined 6 percent year on year, slightly worse than analysts had expected.

items.title: Anthropic may make its S-1 public today
items.sentence: PYMNTS, citing Yahoo Finance, reports Anthropic could publish its IPO prospectus as early as Friday, which would clear the way for a November listing.

items.title: Anthropic's quarterly revenue reaches $16.8 billion
items.sentence: The Motley Fool reports third-quarter revenue rose to $16.8 billion from $11.5 billion with a second straight adjusted-profitable quarter, while OpenAI has pushed its own listing out to 2027.

items.title: DHS orders DeepSeek off federal civilian systems
items.sentence: BleepingComputer reports a Federal Register notice published October 20 requires civilian agencies to remove DeepSeek products, including third-party services built on its technology, with exception requests due within 60 days.

items.title: Nvidia's 64GB DGX Spark ships today
items.sentence: StorageReview reports the $4,999 desktop box goes on sale October 23 through six PC makers, with two units pooling to 128GB of unified memory over ConnectX-7 for models up to 200 billion parameters.

items.title: Bitcoin slips below $82,000 on ETF outflows
items.sentence: Crypto.news reports bitcoin fell under $82,000 after failing to hold $84,000, as US spot ETFs saw $635 million of net outflows on October 22, the largest single day since June 25 and the end of three inflow sessions totaling about $1.08 billion.
